explanation: Olympic velodromes are usually 250 metres a lap, with bends banked at more than 40 degrees. Track bikes have one fixed gear and no brakes.

claims.text: A velodrome is the banked oval track used for track cycling.
A hippodrome is for horse racing, an aerodrome for aircraft and an autodrome for motor racing.
Velodromes used for the Olympics have a lap of 250 metres.
The bends of an Olympic velodrome are banked at more than 40 degrees.
Track racing bikes have one fixed gear and no brakes.
